answers.q1: pnpm (a monorepo; the root package.json pins pnpm@12.9.1 and a preinstall hook rejects npm and yarn). Node must be ^20.19.0 or >=22.12.0. Install with: pnpm install
answers.q2: pnpm run test. This runs test-unit, test-serve and test-build in turn. CI also runs test-serve-bundled, and runs `pnpm run build` first. The e2e tests need Chromium: pnpm playwright install chromium
answers.q4: pnpm run build && pnpm run lint && pnpm format && git diff --exit-code && pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run test-docs. CI's lint job runs these in order. It builds first, then runs eslint (`pnpm run lint`). It then runs the oxfmt formatter (`pnpm format`), and `git diff --exit-code` fails if formatting changed anything. Last come `pnpm run typecheck` and `pnpm run test-docs`. The repo has no .git directory, so the git diff step will not work here.
answers.q5: Do not hand-edit pnpm-lock.yaml, packages/*/CHANGELOG.md (generated by release tooling) or the git-ignored build output (**/dist, **/dist-ssr, playground-temp/, temp/, node_modules, .eslintcache, docs/.vitepress/cache). packages/vite/LICENSE is generated by the build and is also git-ignored. patches/ holds pnpm patch files, so change them with `pnpm patch` and not by hand. packages/vite/src/types/*.d.ts are hand-written type shims for dependencies, so they are not generated.

q1.reason: Says pnpm and gives `pnpm install`, matching the accepted command.

q2.reason: Gives `pnpm run test`, which is accepted, and correctly notes the CI build step, test-serve-bundled and Chromium requirement.

q3.reason: `pnpm exec vitest run <file>` is explicitly accepted and the path is correct.

q4.reason: Includes `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm format && git diff --exit-code`, plus typecheck and test-docs, matching CI; the extra build step is harmless.

q5.reason: Names pnpm-lock.yaml plus generated CHANGELOG.md and git-ignored dist output; the claim that src/types/*.d.ts are hand-written shims is wrong but it doesn't declare any rejected directory generated, and the accept criteria are met.
